stocks.headline: Morning call: right. CEO Jensen Huang is out. The stock fell 4.3% to 166.19 on 4.4x normal volume, touched a 52-week low of 148.80, then closed near the day's high.
stocks.why: This is a people problem and not yet a business problem. Sales are up 106%, the operating margin is 65%, and next year's profit forecasts rose 24% in 90 days. The stock now trades at 10.3x next year's profit, its cheapest in 5 years. The rebound from 148.80 to a close near 167.14, on very heavy volume, looks like forced sellers being cleared out. The real risk is the probe: reports tie Huang's personal links to a Huawei-linked investor, and an outside law firm is investigating. If that turns into export-control or China trouble, it hits sales, not just sentiment. The fallout also reaches AMD (gaining share of investor money), TSM, MU, SMCI and AVGO (suppliers), and CRWV and ORCL, where the market is now questioning AI financing.

long_term.reason: The business is accelerating and the price is the cheapest in 5 years. Brokers cut targets (Goldman to 220, BMO to 240, Citi to 225) but kept Buy ratings, so they are not abandoning the stock.

stocks.what_would_change_it: News that the probe found leaked technology or lost customers, or a weak outlook with no named CEO on Nov 17, would turn this into Avoid.
